Gaussian functions have been extensively utilized in spatial statistics for creating correlated random effects in graphical models, with various extensions proposed to incorporate nonstationarity and heavy-tailed correlations. This work introduces a new class of functions called Mat\'ern M-well-defined functions, which provide both theoretical validity and practical applicability in these contexts. Specifically, the Mat\'ern functions can serve as precise and flexible building blocks in precision specifications that facilitate reliable and efficient likelihood computation, even for large graphs, using an algorithm called Gaussian elimination with backward substitution (GEBC). This paper demonstrates the efficacy of the Mat\'ern functions in multiple scenarios, including their application in dynamic settings and their connection to commonly used functions like the M\'alardale functions.

The growth of cities significantly affects their inhabitants and necessitates accurate assessment and planning. With rapid urbanization occurring worldwide, observing and analyzing metropolitan areas becomes crucial for comprehending how cities are developing. Identifying metropolitan road networks from traffic data helps in detecting areas with heavy road networks, indicating the presence of multiple populations commuting within the city. We propose a new method to detect metropolitan road networks by first defining a metric called Optimal Detection Value (ODV) and presenting an efficient algorithm to maximize it. We apply this algorithm to dataset from Los Angeles, efficiently detecting the metropolitan road network within a reasonable time frame.

By combining experimental data from Belle and KEKE regarding the $J/\psi\to (\gamma + ){\rm invisible}$ decay with theoretical calculations of neutrino and dark energy interactions, a highly constrained upper limit of $1.68 \times 10^{-6}$ has been established for the relevant coupling constant $\varepsilon$. This limit corresponds to an effective scale of at least $1.84 \times 10^{-4}$ eV$^2$/meV$^2$, which sets a minimum value for the Planck mass of the weak gravitational U(1) gauge boson associated with neutrinos and the Einstein-Aether field responsible for dark energy.

Traditional methods for solving differential equations rely on consistent step sizes, 
whereas our proposed approach allows step sizes to vary dynamically. This new 
strategy results in semi-discrete implicit schemes with varying step sizes that 
maintain implicit characteristics and stability guarantees. We demonstrate the 
efficacy of our method with several common test cases, including population 
growth/decay, damped harmonic oscillators, and radioactive decay processes.

Evaluating functional spectra in multiple dimensions is crucial in spectral geometry, especially when employing methods like SSR to handle a large number of modes. This paper presents comprehensive numerical results using two distinct models, offering a public dataset for future research. It also presents an effective SSR configuration for handling multiple modes, leading to accurate spectral analysis.

Autoevaluative Strategies (AES) in hyperparameter optimization are designed to adapt search processes in real-time and automate it. Due to their design, they are highly dependent on historical information and relatively less on performance-based feedback, which makes them prone to both excessive stability and excessive sensitivity. These two extremes are adverse because they restrict the AES's ability to adapt to changes in optimization landscapes, making it crucial to ensure they are neither too stable nor too sensitive. Researchers are urged to employ evaluative measures that are well-balanced and provide a clear-cut evaluation of autoevaluated systems' efficiency.

In higher-dimensional spaces, random walkers who move between adjacent sites eventually separate and never reunite, but in one-dimensional space, they take an infinite amount of time to do so. This infinite time can be thought of as the time it takes for an independent random walker pair to permanently break apart for the first time. However, it also represents the initial period during which they remain connected and move as a single entity. We explore the statistical properties of this initial period, denoted as the joint survival probability of the walker pair, across different dimensional spaces, with a specific emphasis on spaces from one to three dimensions. In addition, we investigate the impact of introducing a small drift into the movement of the walker pair in one, two, and three-dimensional spaces, as well as the effect of starting the walker pair at the same location. For the case where the walker pair begins displaced from each other, we derive exact results for the joint survival distribution in one and two-dimensional spaces, along with precise moments up to the third order for three-dimensional space. The results for the dislocated walker pair can be applied to understand the duration of extreme values in red noise time series. Conversely, the results for the walker pair starting together can help analyze the lifetime of synchronized metronomes coupled through a common noise.

Plasmas an order of magnitude hotter than present fusion-relevant conditions 
can be obtained through power density increases in plasma resonant structures. 
However, the limits of these structures in medium-sized devices have already 
been reached, necessitating a re-evaluation of their design to achieve higher 
power densities. A novel concept called Inertial Static High-Temperature Arc 
Resonator was proposed to break this power density limit, and a traditional 
helicon plasma generator has been used to validate its concept. We analyzed the 
plasma characteristics of an IShTAR plasma generator operating in helicon mode 
by comparing theoretical and experimental measurements of plasma density, 
temperature, and potential. Our analysis revealed that the plasma parameters 
vary radially, with higher values found near the device center, and also showed 
disagreements between theoretical and experimental results likely attributed 
to inaccuracies in theoretical model assumptions such as ignoring plasma 
losses, inaccuracies in superdensity calculations, and assumptions about 
sheath thickness. We derived a corrected electron fluid equation and found that 
this, along with revised losses and potential, can accurately describe the 
plasma density and improve the helicon mode validation of the IShTAR plasma 
generator.

In microbial pesticide systems, a key factor is using a non-pathogenic bacterial strain as an carrier for the virus, which is released into the environment upon the bacteria's death and goes on to infect a target pest species. This strategy is also applicable in a microbial pesticide system involving a parasitoid wasp whose success can be compromised by superseding it with a entomopathogenic fungal strain, which is administered after the wasp has exited its host and before it emerges as an adult wasp. Two models were created to evaluate the efficacy of this symbiotic relationship between an endoparasitoid wasp and an entomopathogenic fungus within the target pest species, considering various scenarios including the bacteria's impact on the micro-organisms and the pest species, as well as the conditions under which wasp offspring can survive. A theoretical model was then developed to analyze data from a pilot study involving the combination of the entomopathoid wasp, the entomopathogenic fungus and a milk bacteria strain, which was found to enhance the longevity and fungal attachment success in adult insects while extending the lifespan of wasp offspring when released into the environment.

A high-quality histopathology dataset is being collected and analyzed by researchers at Aalto University, using light microscopy images and AI technology to annotate the nuclei in a series of H&E stained slides. While some phases of this project are already complete, a significant portion involves creating a robust nucleus annotation tool and training a nucleus detection model with the help of deep learning techniques. Specifically, a novel algorithm is being developed to accurately detect and annotate nuclei in the images, with a particular focus on creating the H-Lambda Mask Model. Additionally, research results show the successful use of a two-stage convolutional neural network in efficiently identifying nuclei in histopathology images, with a high level of accuracy at a specific IOU threshold.

In this study, we extend the concept of a local converse theorem to a specific scenario within the framework of odd symplectic and orthogonal groups in local function fields with a non-zero characteristic. Specifically, we establish that, for a non-trivial character, the symmetry or orthogonality type, and the isomorphism class of an irreducible generic representation determine its underlying Whitteland character, and structure, within their respective local fields. This result is established through an integration of Tate's local duality and the established connections between representations and form factors. Additionally, we leverage recent findings by Cai and Soudry to extend a previous result by Matringe, Shahidi, and Tsimerman, which was limited to representations of higher than zero characteristic.

This research paper proposes two graph parameters, a graph G is considered to have a certain property if its iterated line graph meets specific criteria, and if G possesses a certain level of density, it would have a certain index. We have proven that graphs with a certain density would have a certain index, and if it's a certain type of graph, it would have an optimal hamiltonian pathway. This paper provides an improved proof for a previously established result, and a proof for another result.

The mechanisms underlying SARS-CoV-2 induced pyroptosis remain poorly understood due to a lack of high-quality experimental data for analytical study. Establishing a comprehensive once-cell infection model is proposed to investigate the causes and effects of pyroptosis, as well as the potential interventions available. This model reveals the self-amplifying nature of the inflammatory response through the consumption of cellular inhibitors and the release of inflammatory mediators, ultimately leading to cell lysis. According to the model, pyroptotic cells may contribute to organ failure via pyroshadow effects, which involve the disruption of the blood-brain barrier and subsequent release of inflammatory mediators. The model also highlights the critical role of therapy timing and intervention rate in preventing pyroptosis, with later treatments having limited efficacy. Specifically, the model suggests that steroid therapies can mitigate pyroshadow releases and slow the inflammatory mediators' growth, with complete cell survival possible given optimal conditions.

External state variables and inaccurate incentive signals can hinder reinforcement learning systems, causing them to learn unwanted behaviors and become difficult to manage. External state variables may include unobservable factors that influence the visible state or reward, or they could be difficult to control and predict. In the context of reinforcement learning with multiple agents, external state variables and inaccurate incentive signals can lead to the emergence behavior and thereby undermine the factors mentioned above. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a new approach to identify and remove difficult external state variables and incentive signals by analyzing the distribution of emergent behaviors. This approach ensures that all agents' strategies are focused on achieving the same goal and receiving the same reward. The approach is tested successfully in applications such as reinforcement learning with hidden states and reinforcement learning with contextual bandits.

Consensus-based blockchain protocol Specifications in languages like Smart Contracts require rigorous verification to prevent costly mistakes. In languages with static typing, a powerful technique for static program analysis is the use of refinement types. This paper introduces a novel approach to integration of refinement types in the Tezos smart contract language Spec, which allows for static analysis of programs defined by BNF grammars. Our approach is inspired by the Helium system, but we develop a unique interpretation of refinement types that accounts for the cyclic nature of BNF grammar specifications. We implement this approach in a validator called HELMHOLTZ, which works with Spec specifications.

Due to their effectiveness, Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs) are widely utilized for their versatility, but the internal workings of the graph convolutional layer remain unclear. A key component of GCNNs, the graph convolutional layer, can be equivalent to a matched filter, which involves dividing a input graph's features by the Laplacian smoothness norm before comparing them to the kernel's features. This comparison enables GCNNs to automatically decide the graph features and the kernel features simultaneously. A practical application of this theory involves deconstructing popular GCNN architectures like KGCNN and GraphSAGE, revealing their implicit operations on the input features and their learning of the kernel features. Moreover, this comprehension allows for explicit design of new models with tailored graph convolutions, including multi-head and dilated graph convolutions.

We find a link between gravity and a scalar field by deriving three-dimensional Einstein-Cartan equations from a specific $U(1)\times U(1)$ Chern-Simons-Gross-Neveu model. This model incorporates a complex scalar field with non-trivial self-interactions and reduces to the Einstein-Maxwell theory in three dimensions at a non-zero curvature constant $\Lambda$ and zero spin connection field strength. We then find an anti-de Sitter-like scalar field configuration in the presence of non-zero $\Lambda$, and demonstrate that the Chern-Simons-Gross-Neveu equations of motion can be reduced to general relativity equations in the presence of a non-zero scalar field. We also describe a class of black hole solutions characterized by a horizon temperature dependent on the curvature constant $\Lambda$, and find solutions with zero temperature and non-zero curvature constant $\Lambda$ which reduce to solitons in the limit of vanishing spin connection field strength.

We investigate a novel duality within this context, which involves transforming the charge of a brane and inverting a non-commutative parameter, in a world where spacetime possesses higher-dimensional non-commutative properties, allowing for the expansion of states carrying two charges and the identification of an inextricable link between dual states through a phenomenon analogous to entanglement. This phenomenon arises from the inability to define precise spacetime positions of multiple branes due to the non-commutative properties, ultimately enabling us to demonstrate that the density matrices of these branes are in fact identical.

A novel technique called Virtual Origin Synthetic Aperture (VOSA) is introduced for image processing in ultrasound elastography, addressing the challenges of strain estimation accuracy and lateral displacement calculation necessary for strain mapping in the depth direction. VOSA enhances strain calculation by mitigating the effects of ultrasound wave diffusion and reflection through the use of a high-frequency, short-pulse ultrasound signal. Elastographic strain is evaluated through a multi-stage approach, initially estimating strain at each pixel using a round-trip ultrasound signal, and subsequently correcting for frequency changes induced by spherical wave propagation. The proposed method's performance was verified via both experimental data from healthy human skin and simulated phantoms consisting of distinct materials. VOSA demonstrated significantly improved strain estimation accuracy, achieving a 3.5 to 5.5 times greater precision compared to traditional OSAs. Furthermore, the linear boundary between materials was clearly identifiable using VOSA, matching the accuracy of maximum likelihood estimation, whereas existing methods like cross-spectral ratio and conventional OSA exhibited biases towards stiffer regions and suffered from spatial distortion.

Algorithms can be effectively communicated through step-by-step instructions, whether verbal or written. Recent advances in machine learning have produced algorithms optimized through demonstration analysis, creating a need to interpret these solutions in a human-comprehensible manner. Conversely, providing humans with consistent tasks has led to the development of tools capable of capturing human reasoning, but these solutions often suffer from variability and reliability issues. To address this challenge, our proposed framework for "Rational Pseudocode" connects human demonstrations with algorithmic solutions, allowing for the effective transfer of knowledge between the two. This framework consists of three key components: a method for generating plausible intermediate steps, a method for utilizing these intermediate steps to inform the algorithm, and a method for transferring the underlying reasoning from human to machine. Our model was thoroughly evaluated through three distinct approaches to ensure its effectiveness, including processing从未见过的 input data, adapting to individual user preferences, and effectively transferring the underlying reasoning through the use of targeted questioning.

A Boolean poset $\mathcal{B}_n$ is formed by indexing subsets of $\{1, 2,..., n\}$ according to their size. This paper proves that for any infinite set of shapes, there exists a sufficiently large Boolean poset $\mathcal{B}_n$ that contains each shape as a majorized subset within $\langle \leq n \rangle 2$. This result indicates that Ramsey properties for orderide embeddings in infinite Boolean posets differ significantly from those in infinite natural numbers. Furthermore, the paper establishes that $\mathcal{B}_n$ cannot contain $S$-shaped chains for any configuration $S$ that comprises at least three distinct chains, in contrast to its infinite counterpart which does contain such $S$-shaped chains for all countable configurations $S$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the Boolean posets $\mathcal{B}_n$ do contain infinite chains of specific structural characteristics but cannot contain infinite chains of another specific characteristic.

In the dynamic setting, data points arrive sequentially and can also be removed, presenting challenges due to potential input space expansions without free parameter tuning. Our research offers a dynamic algorithm that effectively manages space by maintaining a random sample of inputs and adapting to changes, either in additions or deletions. This approach yields a set of means representing approximately $O(\sqrt{Opt + D})$ times the optimal cost, where $Opt$ denotes the optimal cost of means centered on actual data points, with the algorithm's sample size growing slowly.

We investigated a novel class of hierarchical stochastic pursuit-escape games on finite graphs, where the lower-level players optimize their outcomes through a probabilistic approach, and a higher-level player strategically selects an edge to maximize or minimize the long-term average result. The concept of a Nash equilibrium in this level-of-game framework leads to narrow intervals of possible game payoffs, and we demonstrated that certain conditions can be met to make these intervals collapse to specific values, effectively decomposing the finite graph into smaller subcomponents with distinct payoff values. Comprehending this decomposition is valuable for analyzing transient behaviors in finite stochastic systems. A particular application involved examining the expected duration of these systems until they reach a target state, where we showed that certain conditions can be made to met to met to met to met to met to met to actually decompose the graph into subcomponents with distinct expected durations; this helps analyze complex scenarios by breaking them into simpler parts.

You're about to encounter nonintuitive findings related to circular likelihoods and nontransitive likelihoods. Consider three options, let's call them A, B, and C, and suppose that in a given scenario, the probability of preferring A to B is higher than the probability of preferring B to C. Interestingly, it's now possible, according to a recent study, that the probability of preferring C to A is even higher, potentially exceeding the initial A vs. B likelihood. However, this seems to contradict the established understanding that increased probabilities should follow a consistent, transitive pattern. Contrary to this, researchers have discovered that circular and nontransitive relationships between options can exist, where the probability of preferring one option over another can vary in an unpredictable, intransitive manner. This discovery holds true regardless of whether the options are comparable or not, and holds across different contexts, including economic exchanges. Furthermore, researchers have identified that such behavior becomes more common as the number of involved options grows. As the number of pairs increases, the likelihood of observing challenging, nonlinear relationships between options should also rise. This should be particularly noticeable in situations like rock-paper-scissors games, where each move counters the previous one, creating a cyclical, nontransitive dynamic.

Recently, deep learning techniques have gained popularity in low-dose CT image denoising due to their robust noise reduction capabilities. However, switching neural network architectures when training models leads to performance degradation and efficiency issues. In this research, we introduce the AdaSwitch LDC network, which combines AdaSwitch modules with a cycle-consistent autoencoder. This novel architecture allows for the seamless switching of encoder and decoder modules to the corresponding low-dose and high-dose networks, thereby preventing degradation and facilitating the training of an end-to-end low-dose CT denoising model. The proposed model was tested on seven datasets and showed superior denoising results compared to the conventional switching GAN.

Recently, large pre-trained models have gained significant popularity in various conversational tasks. However, there's widespread concern that excessive contrastive pre-training may diminish their effectiveness. To address this issue, we introduced a novel, hierarchical contrasting pre-training method known as SPACE-n (where n denotes the number of simultaneous comparisons). In this approach, a single dialog element is paired with a comprehensive set of的组合 dialogs, formed by combining high- and low-value dialogs, at each training step. We conducted experiments using the MultiWOZ 2.0 dataset and found that our proposed method outperformed other contrasting pre-training methods, achieving state-of-the-art results in multiple conversational tasks without requiring significant increases in training data volumes. Notably, our approach surpassed the best existing result, which relied on extensive contrasting pre-training with over 16 million samples per domain.

To understand a ideal fluid spacetime, we first need to discuss the conditions under which its Ricci tensor is conformal to the covariant derivative of its Yamabe scalar and overall, when its Weyl curvature is equal to zero. Once we have these conditions, we can then analyze whether the spacetime is conformal to its Ricci tensor is a gradient soliton and determine its geometric properties in relation to its Yamabe scalar. Additionally, we can verify whether the spacetime satisfies certain mathematical equations, such as its Ricci tensor satisfying a specific relationship with its Yamabe scalar under the condition that its Weyl curvature is equal to zero.

Research on the decoupling spin halos in decoupled halo nuclei has yet to examine spinning distorted halos. A decoupling spin halo is predicted when the core's spin decoupled particles form a spin decoupled particle halos. A decision-coupled particle halo was previously understood through the decoupled Cooper pair effect, and a previous study showed that a decoupling spin halo can exist in spinning double decoupled particle halos, such as $^{38}$Ar. However, a decoupling spin halo cannot form in single decoupled particle halos due to the strong centrifugal force. Instead, a new phenomenon is proposed and called a decision-coupled pair effect. This new phenomenon can lead to a spin decoupled particle halo with an aligned angular momentum on one side of a decoupling particle halo with opposite spatial distributions, which can exist in spinning double decoupled particle halos, and may occur in certain nuclei like $^{42}$Ca, $^{44}$Ti, $^{46}$Sc, $^{48}$Sc, and $^{40}$Ar. A decision-coupled pair effect can also manifest in single decoupled particle halos that can exist in certain nuclei such as $^{48}$Sc and $^{40}$Ar, and the characteristic of a decision-coupled pair effect can be observed through a decision-coupled particle-hole distribution and a

In the video super-resolution field, our proposed model BasicVSR++ builds upon the success of its predecessor, BasicVSR, by incorporating linear transmission layers and aligned network structures. These improvements accelerate convergence during training, allowing the model to effectively utilize a larger dataset, thereby significantly reducing the need for extensive parameter tuning. Furthermore, the influence of rotationally symmetric networks in Video Translation is investigated, revealing their beneficial impact on performance. When combined with linear transmission layers, this approach yields superior results compared to the original BasicVSR and other leading methods on publicly available benchmarks.

The CMS experiment at the LHC utilized 35.6 fb of data, involving dimuon events with central triggers and single-photon candidates, to precisely measure $\theta_{nn}$ distributions in the forward niche. By focusing on events containing isolated photons and semi-isolated muons that satisfy specific kinematic criteria in the forward region, we obtained high-purity samples for both neutral vector bosons. Leveraging the entire dataset, we demonstrated that these backgrounds can be effectively utilized to measure $\theta_{nn}$ with unprecedented statistical power, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of the high-$\eta$ MUON muon scattering process beyond previous limitations, as detailed in the corresponding publication (arXiv:2302.00281).

The issue of catastrophic interference persists in driving the development of multi-task learning models, especially in reinforcement learning (RL) settings, and we investigate this issue from a system design standpoint. Our analysis suggests that model-based multi-task RL systems are inherently susceptible to interference due to their shared structure of models, policies, and data, and we suggest a modular approach to these systems for effective multi-task learning. We introduce two novel strategies to enhance the efficiency of learning in multi-task RL scenarios: firstly, we suggest training distinct subsystems for unrelated tasks to isolate interference, and secondly, we suggest unplugging overtrained modules to maintain stability. We validate our approach on continuous multi-task RL tasks, achieving successful concurrent learning of two tasks without interference, and when applied to real-world robot operations, our proposed system demonstrates an ability to learn and execute newly operated robots after initial disruption.

In this research article, we provide a method to derive a specific approximation scheme involving a parameter $\m$ on a complete, non-compact metric measure space that has a bounded region. This scheme is thought to mimic complex processes of diffusion. For a given function $f$ within a particular space and a complete, non-compact metric measure space that has a bounded region, we think of $\m$ as representing the dimension of the underlying space. This is consistent with Ostrovsky's earlier observations. Our main contributions include showing that, for most values of $\m$ greater than or equal to $n$, solutions $\m$-times equivalent to $ff^\m$ converge strongly to a unique solution $ff$ in the space $L^1(Y,f)$ as $\m$ approaches infinite. This convergence occurs even though the concept of a bounded Laplacian falls apart in infinite-dimensional spaces. Moreover, we derived a complete non-compact version of a specific equation related to quadratic growth. This equation was previously addressed by several researchers but with the underlying space being compact. Our results extend these previous outcomes.

We provide a unified framework for Godel's First Incompleteness Theorem, Godel's Second Incompleteness Theorem, Tarski's Theorem on the Non-Definability of Truth, the First Paradox of Formal Systems, and the Generalized Second Theorem of Incompleteness for Godelian systems, as well as Carnap's Principle of Tolerance. Specifically, if we have a Godelian formal system S that can express basic arithmetic and includes a sentence g claiming its own provability in S, then any set of initial axioms A that does not lead to contradictions within S and guarantees the consistency of S will cause g to be a theorem within the system S. This unified theorem directly implies the First and Second Theorems of Incompleteness, Tarski's Theorem on the Non-Definability of Truth, and Carnap's Principle of Tolerance, but does not imply the First Paradox of Formal Systems. We also explore whether the first sentence of R. Smullyan's Claimed Consistency Theorem satisfies the Godelian condition.

In Clifford analysis, an integral formula known as the Borel-Pompeiu formula exists, which leads to representation formulas for pre-Dirac and Dirac operators. Specific integral Dirac operators, denoted as $T_1$, $T_2$, and $T_3$, can be defined to map from Dirac polynomials in a domain $\Omega$ to Clifford polynomials in $\Omega$. A function can be identified as an eigenfunction of the Dirac operator if it satisfies the equation $Df_\lambda = (|\lambda| + n - 1)f_{-\lambda}$, with a unique entire eigenfunction family existing for each dimension $n \ge 1$. We derive a representation for the eigenfunction $f_\lambda$ using $T_1$, $T_2$, and $T_3$ and an original differential identity involving $D$, $T_1$, $T_2$, and $T_3$. A key identity is established, which, when $\lambda$ is an integer greater than or equal to $n-1$, allows $f_\lambda$ to be completely characterized by its values on the boundary of a domain $\Omega$.

This study stands out as the first instance of analyzing consecutive Markov chain Monte Carlo methods in spatial montecarlo sampling. Building on an independent sampling algorithm from a previous Markov chain, we introduce a new, consecutive algorithm using data from the previous iteration's Markov chain. Both algorithms were evaluated through ideal and real-world data sets involving location of whales and moths in the UK. Comparative results demonstrate the proposed consecutive algorithm to be more space and/or time efficient than its independent counterpart.

Robotic eye-in-hand cameras benefit greatly from optical center correction, a process made easier when the camera is guided by its programmed degrees of freedom. However, this initial setup typically requires multiple images and complex calibration procedures. Our approach diverges from these methods by requiring only a single image and eliminating the need for calibration altogether. Leveraging only one distorted image and the corresponding robotic configuration, our method automatically compares the detected lines in the scene to their expected straight paths if the scene were plane-based, thereby iteratively adjusting the camera's internal parameters until the best match is achieved. This novel technique has been successfully demonstrated with real-world testing involving a ALOHA eye-in-hand camera mounted on a FrankaEmika robotic arm.

In statistical inference tasks, particularly when dealing with ill-posed inverse problems, our objective is to recover an original input $x$ from a given observation $y$ that has been transformed by an unknown function $f$. Given the available data $(y,f)$, our goal can be expressed as finding $x$ such that $y=f(x)$. This paper explores methods to learn the conditional distribution $p(\cdot|y,f)$ in order to generate multiple valid solutions for $x$, rather than just a single optimal answer. To accomplish this, we propose modeling $p(\cdot|y,f)$ as a conditional Markovian random field $\pi(x|y,f)$ and utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to sample from this distribution. A key innovation presented in this paper is the incorporation of a smoothing prior, specifically Brownian motion, into the discriminative loss function of the network, which plays a significant role in enabling the use of stochastic gradient methods, commonly employed in conventional modeling approaches. Additionally, this proposed method addresses the challenge of backward training, a known difficulty in distinguishing training samples from generated samples. Experimental results, conducted with both synthetic data and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images corrupted by motion, demonstrate the method's validity.

Linear mappings can simplify certain dynamical systems, allowing for complex equilibrium analysis. However, applying this technique to systems with non-integer time derivatives poses challenges, as standard transformation rules no longer hold. Despite this, certain researchers have successfully used the linear transformation technique to obtain simplified models and identified key dynamics in specific polynomial algebraic systems. In contrast, we demonstrate through a rigorous mathematical approach that an invariant plane cannot exist in a particular three-dimensional system characterized by fractional order derivatives, regardless of the derivatives behavior near the equilibrium point. Additionally, we generalize this finding to a broader class of similar systems.

Next-generation wireless communication systems must overcome distance limitations by utilizing short-range, high-bandwidth Terahertz frequencies. This necessitates the exploration of multi-hop wireless paths, which however, come with the complication of variable beam training overhead due to the different beam widths and gains available at Terahertz frequencies. Our proposed beam training protocol tackles these challenges by leveraging learnable wide beams at Multi-Pass devices to identify optimal end-to-end wireless links through reinforcement learning. A convolutional neural network at Base Station devices then leverans this information to beam train direct links through the use of narrow beams. Field trials demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in various scenarios.

Pulsar scintillation can serve as a tool for studying the interstellar medium surrounding it, as it arises from the effect of diffraction on radio waves emitted by the compact object, which has passed through turbulent plasma in space. This phenomenon manifests as rapid fluctuations in the pulsar's brightness over time, known as scintillation time. A detailed analysis of the interstellar medium along the path from pulsar B1133+16 to the Earth has been conducted, as this path passes through multiple galaxy components in the Conical region, including its base, middle, and tip. Variations in the scintillation time were observed in different observing sessions, as these occur on a monthly scale, but the differences in the scintillation time did not correspond to the distinct densities of the spiral arms. This suggests that large-scale structures in the galaxy's interstellar medium may not significantly influence its radio waves. Instead, local environments may have a more substantial impact on radio wave propagation, as the variations in scintillation time were also affected by the motion of the Milky Way and the Local Group of galaxies through the cosmos, as this movement passes through the dark matter halo, which undergoes expansion and contraction.

This paper proposes a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to effectively capture the quasi-periodic characteristics of speech signals. By analyzing mel-spectrograms, we observe the periodic structure related to pitch and utilize this insight in our proposed model. Unlike traditional WaveNet models that focus on filtering random signals, Quiperious Autoregressive (QP) models are better suited to human speech due to their quasi-periodic nature. We expand the unit-scale receptive field of dilated convolutional filters while preserving the probability distribution, similar to WaveNet, but with a twist. This technique minimizes Kullback-Leibler divergence and enables the model to directly output speech waveforms from mel-spectrograms, effectively reducing artifacts. Experimental results show that Quiperious Autoregressive Networks outperform dilated WaveNet models in terms of performance.

Historically, Arabic annotation resources have been scarce compared to those for Western languages, largely due to the region's lower technological advancement. Recent technological progress has begun to mitigate this disparity. Our new annotation platform, MADARi, enables accurate, context-sensitive morphological annotation and spelling adjustment for classical Arabic texts, building upon earlier initiatives. Unlike its predecessors, which relied on limited unigram markers, our system incorporates a user-friendly interface incorporating unique features tailored to the Arabic script.

This paper outlines a mathematical model that calculates how ultraviolet and visible light from host stars are absorbed by atmospheric chemicals in exoplanets, providing a framework for analyzing spectral data to determine atmospheric composition and temperature. The model is capable of processing high-density lights that cause the excited state of atoms/molecules and subsequent emission, and it is shown through comparative analysis to yield accurate results consistent with observational data for various types of planets. The study specifically focuses on the photochemistry of temperate and highly atmospheric planets in the M-type star Kepler-42, and it predicts the spectral characteristics of these planets, particularly in the ultraviolet range, where atmospheric composition significantly impacts their appearance. The analysis reveals that the high atmospheric density can lead to enhanced emission features, which can shape the overall spectral profile of these planets.

The search for topological superconductivity has gained significant momentum with the potential to find a Majorana mode in a Josephson junction's zero bias peak (ZBP) in recent experiments on topological superconductors. However, bi-directional tunneling can be influenced by random environment noise in the underlying system, potentially causing anomalous conductance peaks that could be mistaken for the Majorana peak. A comprehensive non-equilibrium statistical field theory has been established to fully describe the physics occurring within the system and its surroundings. Notably, it was demonstrated that the environment-induced peak's shape and amplitude are solely dependent on the dissipation-induced barrier and the conductance at a zero bias will approach $2e^2/h$ as the dissipation increases, whereas the Majorana peak amplitude would be half this value in the high dissipation limit. These distinct differences in peak behavior can be utilized to differentiate the Majorana peak from the environment-induced peak.

Achieving optimal road safety and comfort relies on effective infrastructure maintenance. However, the vast expanse of highways makes manual flaw detection impractical due to its time-consuming and labor-intensive nature. The development of a smart system called RoadAtlas addresses this challenge by creating a user-friendly interface for integrating diverse flaw identification methods and managing the resulting data. The RoadAtlas system automatically collects visual and auditory information through onboard cameras and recording devices during road inspections, which is then processed to pinpoint various infelicities. The system's architecture features a modular design that facilitates the seamless addition of new inspection techniques and manages data efficiently. The graphical user interface (GUI) of the system allows inspectors to control the inspection process and view results on a map while leveraging the power of a web-based backend built with Java, Apache, and MySQL technologies. The research behind this system was demonstrated with the incorporation of two inspection techniques: a manual method and an automatic one based on deep learning, specifically using the U^2 full-sequence unsupervised segmentation model.

This investigation presents an exhaustive breakdown of properties related to shadows in bicategories, along with specific examples from 2-categorical prefractals, monoidal categories, and symmetric monoidal categories. Additionally, it showcases the ability to recover key information about a localized bicategory from its shadow-completed variant.

To test sound localization abilities in animals and humans, traditional setups use multiple traps arranged in a circle, allowing creatures to move freely and pinpoint noises. However, using these telescopic distances can lead to inaccurate results due to sounds appearing too small. We propose a novel, user-friendly approach using multiple microphones and speakers placed close together on the floor, enabling precise low-frequency sound localization. This setup overcomes limitations of previous methods and offers several advantages, including utilizing frequencies often blocked by small animal bodies. We demonstrate its effectiveness by successfully pinpointing sounds ranging from 100Hz to 1kHz in live mice.

Recently, Graph Neural Networks have become the primary choice for processing point cloud data due to their versatility and effectiveness. However, most GNN frameworks are designed for oriented graphs, which can result in a loss of important directional information. To address this limitation, we propose a novel type of Graph Neural Network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Network (LoGNN) that utilizes a Lorentzian connectivity to preserve directional information. We also develop a new module, Lorentzian Multi-Perceptron (LoMP), which combines a Lorentzian aggregation with an Eulerian aggregation to efficiently process point cloud data. The LoGNN is a simple and universal module that can be integrated with existing GNN architectures to adapt them for point cloud processing. The experimental evaluation shows that LoGNN outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmark datasets, including ModelNet, ShapeNet, and S3DIS, in both classification and segmentation tasks.

A new type of squeezed state called a stable-state squeeze has been discovered, which is produced in optomechanical systems when light and sound interact non-linearly. Unlike previous findings of stable-state squeezing, this phenomenon occurs in a linear system. This discovery is made possible thanks to a new type of optomechanical interaction called cross-linear coupling, which happens when an optical photon absorbs or emits sound waves, altering the frequency of the optical cavity. Researchers used a forward Raman process to detect this interaction and show that stable-state squeezing can be observed in the case of dominant mechanical modes. This state of squeezing, which exceeds measurement uncertainties, could be achieved in experiments involving human hearing frequencies.

We propose an extension of the scalar mu-calculus called the modal particle mu-calculus, which introduces modal operators susceptible to backification. This new variant enables the representation of system properties in a more concise and intuitive manner. When applied to transition systems, it also enables a more streamlined expression of simulation relations and bisimulations. A further generalization, the modal particle vector mu-calculus, combines features of the modal particle mu-calculus with vector functions, similar to the modal mu-calculus. This additional variant offers an alternative to traditional trace theory, particularly for analyzing non-regular behaviors.

According to the recently introduced concept of effective exponential delay devaluation, a novel framework has now been established to calculate inflation rates influenced by non-renewable resource prices. This framework employs the 'effective price' of a non-renewable resource as its primary indicator, and based on its broader applications in economics and physics, a new mathematical model has been developed using the 1990s-discovered, yet underutilized, Tsallis' power law. The model's general formulation is presented along with specific instances, and the connection between the introduced Tsallis' index and the 'delay parameter' of the delay devaluation model is explicitly defined. Furthermore, a novel relationship has now been discovered between the Tsallis index and the rate at which the economy grows, and the implications of this model on the Fisher equation and the understanding of inflation as a byproduct of declining resources have now arisen.

In the context of harmonically coordinate-transformed gravity, a potential connection to traditional harmonic gauge appears relevant, possibly indicating that specific harmonic gauge conditions correspond to modified gauge constraints within a higher-order gravitational theory. This speculation may be grounded in modifying a theoretical framework that accounts for significant gravity effects, such as those found in the vacuum of space far from massive objects, which could impact fundamental measurements like the speed of light. Although this concept involves consideration of standard general relativity, it aims to consider gravity's potential effects beyond small speed approximations.

Building on recent research by Steger and Timar regarding double covers as maximum homomorphism targets, we have significantly broadened this concept. Our new criteria for expanded double covers as maximum homomorphism targets in signed graphs are much less restrictive than the previous requirements, which heavily relied on statistical limit theory. To demonstrate the power of our criteria, we have significantly increased the range of graph families that have maximum homomorphism targets equivalent to double covers, including cycles, trees, and specific connected tree-like structures. Additionally, our new criteria imply a significant enhancement to a recent result by Thomason and Seress regarding the homomorphism numbers of trees and cycles.

The author explores how different statistical mechanics concepts, such as canonical equilibrium, are represented using Weyl-Wigner formalism, building on the rigorous mathematical foundations established by Fugate and Shigekawa. By utilizing operator theory within a von Neumann algebra framework, the proof demonstrates the convergence of the Weyl-Wigner approximation to canonical equilibrium equilibrium as the Planck constant approaches zero. This convergence rate is further improved in the algebra setting, providing a more precise understanding of the relationship between semiclassical and quantum canonical equilibrium states.

The notion of negative absolute temperature, initially proposed by W. Pauli and later expanded upon by L. Rosenhead, has been the subject of significant speculation. According to statistical mechanics, negative temperatures can theoretically exist within two-level systems, yet such temperatures have never been observed or measured in nature. In actual two-level systems, populations of higher energy states never surpass those of lower energy states, rendering the concept of negative temperature, at best, a theoretical possibility. 

Furthermore, ambiguities surrounding the thermodynamic definition of temperature in the context of systems with bounded spectra contribute to the ambiguity of negative absolute temperature. In fact, systems that exhibit such temperatures would, under certain conditions, align more closely with super-radiant systems. 

Our analysis suggests that, given the limitations of current thermodynamics, negative absolute temperature remains within the bounds of uncertainty and could, in theory, coexist with the law of energy conservation.

Given a positive integer $n$ and a set $A$ consisting of $n$ distinct non-negative integers, let $B$ be the set formed by adding each element of $A$ to another element (can be the same) from $A$. If $A$ contains at least three consecutive integers starting from $0$, we establish a key constraint: for any assignment of signs ($-1$ or $1$) to the elements of $B$, there exists an integer $t$ (between $1$ and $2n-1$) that can be formed in at least $\frac{3n+1}{2n}(n-1)$ ways (as a signed sum of elements from $A$). This representation limit is nearly optimal, representing a improvement over the prior record by a factor of two. Additionally, we derive a similar result close to $2n/\sqrt{n}$ for situations where the representation discrepancy is at least $n$.

The public annotated datasets used in classification tasks are often insufficiently large, particularly in medical applications.  To address this limitation, researchers have been building comprehensive annotated collections for specific medical conditions.  However, the number of resources is still limited, and there is a need for additional datasets to support complex classification problems.  In response to this challenge, the authors present the UniToPatho dataset, which consists of 11873 histopathological images from colorectal polyps.  These images are annotated for basic features like color and texture, as well as more complex classifications like adenoma grading and cancer detection.  The authors believe that this dataset will facilitate research on multi-task classification tasks, and they invite the scientific community to utilize it for this purpose.

By transforming the time-dependent diffusion equation to its steady-state equivalent, a source term $\vec{f}$, a conductivity coefficient $a$ are defined in $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$. The problem seeks to find $u$ in $\Omega$ that satisfies $-{\rm div}(a{\rm grad}\,u) = \vec{f}$ with Neumann boundary conditions ${a{\rm grad}\,u}\cdot\vec{n} = 0$ on the boundary $\partial\Omega$. A novel numerical method is introduced, adapting the standard continuous problem by rescaling the domain using a frequency parameter $\omega$. The modified problem includes an additional term $\omega{\rm div}({a{\rm grad}\,u}) = \vec{f}$ in the equation. Theoretical analysis shows that for a sufficiently large $\omega$, solutions to the standard and adjusted problems converge. This proposed technique leverages existing solvers for second-order elliptic equations to solve RF filter circuits designed for time-invariant signals.

By examining the hydropatite contents of meteorites Chelyabinsk and Benenitra, our analysis indicates a significant water-rich accumulation of dry planetesimals in the inner solar system's background population.  95% of the measured samples from both falls/showers exhibited notable levels of hydropatite content, in contrast to only 5% with insignificant content.  Given the closed-system nature of benenitra and chelyabinsk, their hydropatite contents mirror the water-rich accumulation of dry planetesimals in the inner solar system's background population.  These findings indicate that the process of planet formation in the inner solar system involved a significant stage of dry planetesimals with substantial water content.  This conclusion is in contrast to previous beliefs suggesting that some dry planetesimals formed beyond the snowline and then accumulated into the inner solar system.  In comparison to benenitra and chelyabinsk, the process of planet formation in the inner solar system probably resulted in dry planetesimals with even higher water content.

Using the Bethe-ansatz method, we've calculated the structure factors for a pair of neighboring spins in a XXZ spin chain extending beyond traditional pairs, specifically for excitations involving the s-1 spin and correlators involving the joint J^(s)J^(s) and J^(s)J^(s-1). By analyzing the chain's behavior in its ground state and at low spin correlations, we observe that in the regime where the parameter Delta lies within the range (-1,1), and the chain length approaches infinity, J^(s)(1/2,J^(s)(1/2, expectations can be expressed as a combination of Dirac delta functions, Heaviside step functions, and the Hurwitz zeta function, all of which align with the symmetry possessed by these models. Furthermore, we observe a deep connection with the symmetry of the affine quantum group U_q( sl_2), and we derive an explicit mathematical representation for the Hurwitz zeta function in terms of this quantum-group's symmetry.

This paper zero-shot transfer learning applied to robust audio source separation, tackling scenarios where the training data doesn't match the test data. Unlike typical transfer learning, our approach requires no training on test samples. Initially, we evaluated various zero-shot strategies using the Magnitude spectrum and梅尔倒谱变换 (Mel-spectrogram) representations, ultimately developing a novel method combining both in a linear fashion. Our proposed technique achieved an average improvement of 3.1 dB in Signal-to-Distortion Ratio (SDR) over competing methods, including best-matching and similar dataset approaches. Notably, even when significant acoustic and recording discrepancies existed between training and test samples, our method delivered substantial performance gains of 5.8 SDR points on average compared to standard zero-shot techniques.

Within the dipole approximation, interacting with an incident wave of any wavelength, we've previously developed an algorithm to compute scattering and related quantities by analyzing term-by-term contributions. Now, an expanded version of this algorithm is presented for multipole interactions - specifically up to quadrupole - specifically tailored to metamaterials consisting of unit cells significantly larger than the operating wavelength. Through numerical simulations, we've demonstrated that distinct physical terms contribute to scattering and material responses such as absorption, transmittance, and reflectance in carefully designed scenarios, thus validating our series approach in overcoming the limitations of the scattering matrix element derivation under the condition where the wave number times the lattice constant equals 2/π.

This study introduces two innovative concepts: the double Young-Capelli bitableaux and the Schur altered symmetric functions. Currently, the Schur functions can be expressed as sums of monomial and elementary symmetric functions, specifically using Young and Capelli bitableaux respectively. In contrast, our findings reveal that the Schur altered symmetric functions can also be expanded using Young and Capelli bitableaux.

Within the simplest scoto-seesaw model's framework, we examine the potential for neutrino mass generation, ensuring stability of the electroweak vacuum, and the explanation of dark matter abundance and properties within the Standard Model. By extending the standard Standard Model with two right-handed neutrinos and additional singlet scalars and fermions (dark sector), we can achieve these goals if we adopt a specific extension where the dark sector's symmetry is broken, resulting in WIMP-like dark matter behavior. Phenomenological analysis of this model involves examining dark matter interaction with nucleons and resonance production at the Large Hadron Collider. We find that a viable range of dark matter masses lies between 2 to 10 TeV, allowing for agreement with all cosmological and laboratory observations of neutrino and dark matter densities, as well as nucleon interaction cross-section observable in direct detection experiments. Additionally, identifying right-handed neutrino masses in the 5 to 15 TeV range contributes to the stability of the electroweak vacuum.

The concept of $f$-$d$ orbital hybridization has been established multiple times, resulting in multiple outcomes including total mixing, minimal mixing, or even separation, which has already been discussed in numerous studies.  This has significant implications for the electronic structure of various compounds, including those with multiple orbitals like lanthanides, actinides, and transition metals.  Although the primary focus of this work lies with $f$ and $d$ orbital pairs, understanding the electronic structure of various compounds necessitates a deeper comprehension of the mixing or separation of other orbital pairs, including $d$-$d$, $d$-$p$, and $p$-$p$ orbital pairs.  Despite numerous theoretical models having been developed to explain the behavior of these multiple mixed/separated orbital pairs, there has been a notable lack of theoretical models addressing models of multiple hybridization like $f$-$d$ and $d$-$d$ pairs simultaneously.  To address this knowledge gap, we have presented a theoretical model exploring the blending or separation of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ $d$-orbitals, including a direct $d$-$d$ hybridization, which has already been observed in several 4d and 5d transition metal compounds, including RPtO$_3$ (R = La to Nd), R$_2$PdGa$_8$O$_{24}$ (R = La to Nd), and BaMnAs

This research focuses on rational transformations of non-singular projective varieties, and introduces methods to lift these maps from the algebraic geometry level to the level of the Darboux-Teukolsky metric, and further to the level of quantum homology. New concepts including relative quantum homology, and operations within these frameworks are introduced, and proven to correspond to Chern classes and string operations in the context of quantum homology. A specific application is demonstrated in calculating the quantum cobordism ring of $\mathbb{P}^n$.

In our work, we introduce a novel concept called illness-aware image transformation on thoracic radiographs. Our goal is to enable neural network diagnostics by training them on radiographs depicting accurate anatomical abnormalities. Current diagnoses rely on radiographs annotated with regional notes indicating target organs and pathological conditions. However, to train effective detection or segmentation models, we need radiographs that accurately reflect these regions and conditions. This task poses significant challenges due to variations in real patient images. We propose a strategy to generate anatomically accurate abnormalities by combining real and synthetic data, utilizing masking techniques and pre-trained neural networks. Specifically, we focus on pneumonias and bone fractures as examples. To evaluate our approach, we conducted segmentation and detection tasks for both conditions, outperforming alternative methods in our tests. Our code is available online.

multidimensional representation and visualization technologies are crucial for comprehending complex, real-world data sets, especially in high-dimensional spaces.  One challenge faced by traditional visualization methods is that they often rely on linear representations and can be difficult for domain experts to interpret.  As a result, alternative visualizations have been developed to assist in making sense of intricate patterns and relationships within multidimensional data sets.  However, there is still a lack of advanced tools capable of facilitating a thorough examination of real-world vector data sets, taking into account their underlying distribution and relationships.  To address this need, we created the visual intelligence and diagnostic analysis expert tool (ViDaExpert), an innovative multidimensional visualization system designed for multidomain vector data sets.  This innovative tool integrates diverse visualization techniques, including parallel coordinates and heat maps, to facilitate comprehensive examination and interpretation of real-world vector data sets, allowing users to identify valuable patterns and relationships within complex data sets.

On a flat surface, we can efficiently calculate the Newtonian potential and density at a large number of points using approximately 10 to 100,000 other points, within around 100 to 10,000 seconds. Our proposed simple and accurate method provides a useful alternative to other numerical approaches for solving problems on a two-dimensional flat surface, such as those found in astrophysics and fluid dynamics. Our approach yields highly precise results, with a maximum error of about 3x10^-5 and an average error of about 3x10^-7 for the potential, and a maximum error of about 1.4x10^-5 and an average error of about 6x10^-7 for the density.
